message: Four analytic curves: correlated voters' majority vote saturates below 1 as voters are added, best-of-m selection bias grows only like the square root of two ln m, evidence retention decays geometrically with chain depth, and an irrecoverability rule is a cliff versus graceful degradation.

report.claim: Analytic models, using illustrative parameters and not real data, predict four curve shapes. Correlated voters stop gaining accuracy as their number grows. Picking the best of many candidates inflates the winner's apparent quality. Evidence fades along a chain of compaction stages while adoption of a 'lure' rises when an attractor is present. Two rival hypotheses, a sharp cliff and a smooth decline, predict different accuracy curves as raw evidence is lost.
report.structure: Four panels in a 2x2 grid, each with its own axes and a bold title. (a) and (b) are labelled 'Replication'. (c) is labelled 'Propagation' and (d) 'Irrecoverability'. Panel (a) has dotted lines for the ceilings, and panels (b) and (c) have text annotations. Panel (d) has a dotted vertical line and a dashed horizontal line. No arrows connect the panels.
report.first_look: The black curve in panel (a), which rises steeply and levels off near 0.98. The colored lower curves flatten sooner at their dotted ceilings.
unreadable: In panel (d), the 'r*' label on the dotted vertical line is grey and overlaps the legend text 'H-cliff', so it is nearly hidden.
In panel (d), the legend sits on top of the plotted curves at the lower left.
In panel (c), the grey λ = 0.05, 0.18 and 0.35 labels sit at the right ends of the lines and are small. The lure-adoption curves' lack of direct labels means readers must rely on the legend.
questions: What do 'replication', 'propagation' and 'irrecoverability' mean here, and why are these three grouped together?
What is ρ, and how is correlation between voters defined in the model?
Why does the right-hand y-axis in (b) say 'selection bias in units of σ', and what is a 'candidate' in the underlying setting?
Why does λ = 0.18 get singled out and tied to SimulatedAgent, while 0.05 and 0.35 are shown in grey?
How does the lure-adoption curve relate to the evidence-retention formula in the panel title?
What is the 'retrieval-backed memory: budget floor' at about 0.72 in (d), and why is it drawn as a horizontal line?
What is 'OP-19', and what does it mean to downgrade 'irreversible' to 'costly'?
How are the panel (a) ceiling values, such as 0.95 for ρ = 0.06, obtained?
Why do the (a) curves start at 0.70 for m = 1, and why is m odd only?
